findings.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without optional chaining, so every Google Meet booking made by a user with no destination calendar - exactly the case this fallback exists to handle - throws a TypeError and the whole booking fails.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — deleteEvent's fallback `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only evaluated when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always compares against null, returns undefined and falls back to "primary"; Google replies 404, which the handler swallows with `resolve()`, so cancellation reports success while the event stays on the host's calendar forever.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:76 — Office365 createEvent ignores the credential it was invoked with and always posts to `destinationCalendar[0]`, so in a collective fan-out every Outlook host after index 0 has the event POSTed to another host's calendar id - the feature this PR ships only works for Google.

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:162 — BaseCalendarService (CalDAV/Apple/etc.) still filters its calendars against `destinationCalendar[0]`, so for any host past index 0 the filter matches zero calendars, `Promise.all([])` succeeds, and createEvent returns a fabricated uid - a booking reference is persisted for an event that was never created anywhere.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147 — find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` returns undefined for any DestinationCalendar row whose credentialId is NULL (the exact rows the `else` branch in createAllCalendarEvents exists for), so the event is silently written to "primary" instead of the user's selected calendar and createEvent still resolves with success.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — updateEvent has the same dead `find` (only reached when externalCalendarId is falsy), so calendarId resolves to undefined and the Google update is malformed; the previous fallback to the destination calendar's externalId is gone, breaking reschedule for every booking reference that has no stored externalCalendarId.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:168 — The hangout-link `events.patch` still passes raw `selectedCalendar`, which can now be undefined (only the insert got the `|| "primary"` guard), and the call is neither awaited nor caught - an unhandled promise rejection plus a Meet link that never lands in the description.

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:129 — Lark createEvent hardcodes `destinationCalendar[0]`, so a second Lark host in a collective event has the event created against the first host's calendar id rather than their own.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` is a silent no-op when destinationCalendar is null, so a collective event with no event-type calendar and an organizer who has no destination calendar drops every team member's calendar with no error and falls through to the "first connected calendar" fallback.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts:175 — Confirmation (and the Stripe/PayPal webhook handlers) rebuild destinationCalendar from the single `booking.destinationCalendar` row, so collective events that require confirmation or payment silently keep the old one-calendar behaviour - the fan-out never happens and nothing reports it.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:2124 — Booking success is still judged with `results.every(res => !res.success)`; with N calendar results one success masks N-1 failures, so hosts silently missing their calendar event never surfaces as a booking error.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:2072 — The reschedule path uses `results.some(res => !res.success)`, so a single host with an expired token now fails the entire reschedule and suppresses every reschedule email, even though the other N-1 calendars were updated successfully.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:444 — The recurring-cancel block is now nested inside the per-reference loop, so with N calendar references it re-deletes every remaining booking across every credential N times (N x M Google delete calls); it also still only walks the organizer's credentials, leaving the other hosts' recurring events orphaned.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:590 — return Promise.all(result)` is returned, not awaited, inside the try, so a rejection from any one host's updateEvent bypasses the local catch and 500s the whole reschedule; the promises are also started at line 542 while later iterations still `await prisma.credential.findUnique`, leaving a window with no handler attached (unhandledRejection).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:208 — updateLocation builds new booking references from `result.externalId` / `result.credentialId`, but CalendarManager.updateEvent returns neither field, so every location edit appends a calendar reference with null externalCalendarId and null credentialId, degrading all later cancel/reschedule to the broken "primary" fallback.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:380 — In the no-credentialId branch createEvent is called without the new externalId argument, so the resulting reference loses externalCalendarId (previously taken from `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`), permanently breaking cancel and update for those bookings.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:140 — All N collective inserts reuse the same `conferenceData.createRequest`, and Google mints a fresh Meet link per event, so hosts 2..N see a different Meet URL on their calendar than the one sent to the attendee; the identical attendee list also makes the booker's own calendar show N duplicate invitations.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — The `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` guard on `slug` was inverted (was `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }`), so self-hosted orgs are now created with a null slug while cloud orgs claim the subdomain before payment - an unrelated regression that also lets unpaid users squat org slugs.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:496 — Switching from find to filter on `type.includes("_calendar")` now also matches `*_other_calendar` references, which are then updated a second time by the dedicated other_calendar block below, double-applying updates to CRM integrations.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:987 — Nothing de-duplicates the destination calendars collected here, so two hosts pointing at the same shared calendar (or an event-type calendar equal to a host's) produce two identical events on one calendar plus two references, one of which will later delete the wrong event.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1877 — Only `destinationCalendar[0]` is connected to the Booking row while N calendar events are created, so every downstream rebuild from `booking.destinationCalendar` (confirm, payment webhooks, requestReschedule, deleteCredential) can only ever see one of the N calendars.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:339 — The fan-out awaits each provider call sequentially inside the booking request while references are only persisted at the very end inside a catch-and-log block, so a timeout or a failed reference write part-way through leaves the already-created host calendar events orphaned and invisible to cancellation.

apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249 — destinationCalendar changes from an object to an array in every outgoing webhook payload with no versioning or migration note, silently breaking existing subscribers that read `destinationCalendar.externalId`.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:736 — The rewritten loadUsers drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-booking user select while the result is still cast to IsFixedAwareUser (which declares organization as non-optional), so getBookerUrl loses org context for dynamic group bookings.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:433 — Credentials are now fetched by raw id via `prisma.credential.findUnique` with no ownership check, so a stale or corrupted reference.credentialId makes the cancel path instantiate a calendar client with an unrelated user's OAuth token.

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221 — Calendar.createEvent gains a required credentialId param, a breaking interface change with no optional/default or deprecation path for the app-store implementations.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72 — Office365CalendarService.createEvent was not updated to the new createEvent(event, credentialId) signature and still resolves only destinationCalendar[0], so collective bookings write every host event into the first host calendar.

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:125 — LarkCalendarService.createEvent still has the old one-arg signature and picks destinationCalendar[0], ignoring the credentialId needed to select the correct host calendar.

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:125 — BaseCalendarService.createEvent (CalDAV/Apple and every derived app) was not updated to accept credentialId and filters calendars by destinationCalendar[0].externalId only.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:118 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration is dereferenced without optional chaining, so the new empty-array/null destinationCalendar shape throws a TypeError on Google Meet bookings that the old `?.` handled.

apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:119 — Webhook payload field destinationCalendar flipped from an object-or-null to an array for external subscribers with no API version bump or changelog; only the BOOKING_REJECTED fixture at line 249 was updated while BOOKING_CREATED still expects null.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) silently no-ops when the value is null, dropping every collective host calendar and defeating the stated intent of the change.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:169 — externalCalendarId on the persisted BookingReference now comes from result.externalId, which is undefined for every createEvent call that omits it (lines 380, 391, 403), so references lose the external calendar id used by later update/delete.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — The destinationCalendar fallback in updateEvent matches cal.externalId against externalCalendarId inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always yields undefined and events.update is called with calendarId undefined.
packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — Same dead fallback in deleteEvent: the find() can never match, so deletes silently target "primary" instead of the destination calendar.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1067 — This producer emits null for "no destination calendar" while every other producer emits [], giving webhook consumers three sentinels (null, [], array) for the same field.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:64 — EventManagerUser.destinationCalendar is still the singular DestinationCalendar-or-null type, inconsistent with the new array contract on CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar.

packages/core/builders/CalendarEvent/builder.ts:198 — setDestinationCalendar is a public builder API whose parameter type silently changed to DestinationCalendar array, breaking any out-of-diff caller that passes a single object.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:2296 — The new CalendarEvent.schedulingType field is spread into webhookData via ...evt, leaking internal event-type configuration into external webhook payloads undocumented.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced with no optional chaining, so any Google Meet booking whose event has an empty/null destinationCalendar throws a TypeError on the exact fallback path this branch exists to handle.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — The `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` fallback only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate can never match and `selectedCalendar` becomes undefined; events.update is then called with `calendarId: undefined` instead of the destination calendar.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — Same self-defeating predicate in deleteEvent: the find is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so `calendarId` always falls back to "primary" and events living in a destination calendar are never deleted.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — Condition inverted: `slug` was previously written only when team billing is DISABLED, now it is written only when billing is ENABLED, so self-hosted orgs are created with no slug and billed orgs get a live slug plus requestedSlug before payment.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:208 — updateLocation builds references from `result.externalId` / `result.credentialId`, but CalendarManager.updateEvent returns neither field, so every reference created by a location edit is persisted with null externalCalendarId and credentialId.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — Non-calendar (video) results now get `credentialId: undefined`; previously they used `result.credentialId`, so video booking references lose the credential needed to update/cancel the meeting later.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147 — Calendar selection now keys on `cal.credentialId === credentialId`, so destination calendars with a null credentialId (legacy rows) never match and the event silently lands in "primary" instead of the configured external calendar.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:168 — The hangout-link `events.patch` still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which can be undefined now that the "primary" fallback moved to the insert call, producing a failing unawaited Google API call.

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:161 — CalDAV/Apple createEvent filters calendars by `destinationCalendar[0]` only, so when invoked with a non-first collective host's credential nothing matches, `responses` is empty, `some((r) => !r.ok)` is false and it returns success without creating any event.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Office365 createEvent always targets `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` regardless of which credential it was invoked with, so for a second collective host it POSTs to a calendar id that does not exist under that account.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` silently drops every team destination calendar when the event type and organizer both have none, so collective hosts get no calendar events in exactly the case the PR targets.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:380 — The legacy branch (destination without credentialId) calls `createEvent(c, event)` with no externalId argument, so the resulting EventResult and booking reference carry no externalCalendarId and later updates/deletes target the primary calendar.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:540 — credential` can still be undefined after the DB fallback (credential row missing or `app.slug` null) and is passed straight into updateEvent, which dereferences `credential.appName` and throws.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:592 — The `console.error(message)` was removed from the catch block, so `message` is computed and discarded and all updateAllCalendarEvents failures are now silent.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:445 — The recurring-cancellation block is now nested inside the per-reference loop, so for a collective booking with N calendar references it re-runs the full delete sweep N times, issuing duplicate deleteEvent calls for every remaining booking.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — The recurring path still iterates only `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and `references.find(...)` (first calendar ref), so co-hosts' calendar events created by the new multi-destination write are never deleted.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:597 — When the failure happens before `calendarReference` is assigned the catch returns `[]`; callers such as editLocation.handler guard with `results.length > 0 && results.every(...)`, so a hard failure is now reported as success.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:757 — The new catch-all rewraps every loadUsers failure, downgrading any HttpError to 400 and turning an empty dynamicUserList into a generic 500 instead of the previous 404 eventTypeUser.notFound.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:736 — The dynamic-user query dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` while the result is still cast to IsFixedAwareUser (which declares `organization: { slug: string }`), so any consumer reading `user.organization.slug` for dynamic bookings gets undefined.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — The 18-line `prisma.credential.findUnique` + manual field-by-field Credential remap is copy-pasted verbatim here and at line 517; extract one `getCredentialById` helper or it will silently drift when the Credential model gains a field.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:517 — Second verbatim copy of the credential fetch/remap block from line 344, differing only in `reference.credentialId` vs `destination.credentialId`.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:433 — Third copy of the credential-fallback fetch, but this one omits the `app: { select: { slug } }` include the two EventManager copies use, so the three "same" lookups already disagree on shape.

packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:220 — New optional `externalId` param is never used inside `createEvent` — it is only echoed back onto the result; being optional, the two other call sites (EventManager.ts:380, :391) silently omit it and produce results with `externalId: undefined`.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:592 — console.error(message)` was deleted from the catch but the `message` string is still built and now unused — dead code plus a lost error log in the calendar-update failure path.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1077 — evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` mutates the event after construction, so collective host calendars are silently dropped whenever the literal at line 1063 resolved to `null`; build the full array in one place instead.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:731 — The unrelated `loadUsers` rewrite drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user select while `IsFixedAwareUser` (line 355) still declares `organization: { slug: string }` — a scope-creep change that quietly alters the user shape this whole handler infers from.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — Unrelated scope creep that also inverts behavior: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, flipping when the org slug is persisted.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:255 — event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it can never match — permanently dead lookup that reads as intentional.
packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:316 — Same never-matching `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` in the falsy-`externalCalendarId` branch of `deleteEvent`.

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 — The `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` idiom is hand-rolled at 10+ sites across 6 files with no shared accessor and no documented/enforced "index 0 == main host" invariant.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:118 — This is the only place the "first element is the main host" invariant is written down (in a comment), and nothing enforces it — every other consumer just destructures index 0 and hopes.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:251 — The `x ? [x] : y ? [y] : []` nested-ternary destinationCalendar wrap is duplicated at ~8 call sites (also :528, confirm.handler:175, editLocation:85, deleteCredential:290, paypal-webhook:152, handleNewBooking:1063, requestReschedule:240) while 3 other sites use a different two-step style — no shared `toDestinationCalendars()` helper.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:689 — ["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(eventType.schedulingType)` discards the imported `SchedulingType` enum (still used at line 805), and the stringly-typed comparison then spreads to lines 992, 1021 and 1077.

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221 — createEvent(event, credentialId: number)` pushes caller credential identity into the generic Calendar interface, yet 3 of the 4 implementations ignore the new argument — the boundary now lies about what implementers must handle.
packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:182 — schedulingType` is added to `CalendarEvent` and written in handleNewBooking.ts:1074 but read nowhere in the repo — a write-only field on a widely shared type.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:757 — Unrelated try/catch added around `loadUsers` converts every failure to a generic 500 "Unable to load users"; the `error instanceof HttpError` branch is unreachable since nothing in the try throws one.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:145 — Dangling comment "Find in calEventRaw.destinationCalendar the one with the same credentialId" left floating above a blank line, detached from the code it describes.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:495 — calendarReference` is now a `PartialReference[]` but keeps its singular name, and the catch block at line 597 still reports a `credential` that is whatever the last loop iteration left behind.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:417 — bookingCalendarReference` changed from `find` to `filter` but kept its singular name, so `bookingCalendarReference.length > 0` reads confusingly.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:997 — Hardcoded `firstName: ""` / `lastName: ""` added to team member objects is unrelated to the destinationCalendar change and adds fields no caller populates.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — Recurring-cancel branch now re-runs the full credentials x updatedBookings deleteEvent cross-product once per calendar reference, multiplying external delete API calls by the number of fixed hosts (e.g. 5 refs x 2 creds x 12 remaining bookings = 120 calls instead of 24, most of them duplicates).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:433 — prisma.credential.findUnique is awaited inside the per-calendar-reference loop, a serial N+1 that scales with team size; the ids should be batched into one findMany with id: { in: [...] }.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — createAllCalendarEvents awaits prisma.credential.findUnique once per destinationCalendar entry, adding one serial DB round trip per fixed host on the booking-creation hot path.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:370 — createEvent is awaited serially inside the destinationCalendar for-loop, so external calendar API latency now multiplies by the number of fixed hosts instead of fanning out with Promise.all as the sibling branch does.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:517 — updateAllCalendarEvents awaits prisma.credential.findUnique once per calendar reference, an N+1 that grows with team size on every reschedule/update.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — teamDestinationCalendars is pushed onto evt.destinationCalendar without dedup, so hosts sharing a calendar (or one matching eventType.destinationCalendar) cause redundant createEvent API calls and duplicate calendar entries per booking.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:443 — getCalendar is re-instantiated per reference and again per credential inside the nested recurring loop, repeating calendar-service construction and token handling R x C times per cancellation.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration dereferences undefined whenever destinationCalendar is null/empty, so every Google Meet booking without a destination calendar now throws before any event is created.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:369 — If both the in-memory and DB credential lookups miss (or app.slug is null) the host is skipped with no log and no failure EventResult, so that host's calendar is silently never created and nothing surfaces it.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:370 — Sequential awaited createEvent per host with no try/catch: a throw on host #2 aborts the remaining hosts and leaves host #1's already-created event orphaned with no compensating delete.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:380 — The no-credentialId branch calls createEvent without destination.externalId, so the booking reference stores no externalCalendarId and later update/delete cannot target that host's calendar.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:339 — Fan-out to N host calendars has no timeout or retry around the external calendar API calls, so one hung provider stalls the entire booking request.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:542 — credential may still be undefined after the DB fallback yet is passed to updateEvent, which dereferences credential.appName and rejects, failing the whole update batch.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:590 — Promise.all rejects on the first failing host and the catch then reports every reference as failed even though other hosts' calendars were already updated successfully.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:592 — The removed console.error leaves the computed error message unused, so updateAllCalendarEvents failures are now completely silent.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:480 — credential is declared outside the per-reference loop, so the catch-block message attributes the failure to whichever credential happened to be assigned last.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:160 — evt.iCalUID is reassigned by each calendar result in the map, so with N hosts the last host's iCalUID silently overwrites the others.
packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:243 — The 404 branch returns undefined without logging or setting calError, so a host whose externalId does not match its credential fails with zero diagnostics.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:2124 — results.every((res) => !res.success) only raises an error when every calendar fails, so with N hosts a partial failure is reported to the organizer as a fully successful booking.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — The recurring-event delete branch now re-runs once per calendar reference, issuing duplicate deleteEvent calls for every credential x updated booking.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:470 — deleteEvent promises are pushed without individual rejection handling; any throw before the Promise.allSettled at line 656 (e.g. the payment throw at line 537) turns N in-flight deletes into unhandled rejections.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — The fallback find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) is only evaluated when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always returns undefined and events.update is called with calendarId undefined.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — Same tautological find in deleteEvent makes calendarId fall back to "primary", so a co-host's event is looked up on the wrong calendar, 404s, resolves as success at line 335, and is left orphaned.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:166 — calendar.events.patch is fired without await or catch, so its rejection (now likelier since calendarId can be undefined) becomes an unhandled promise rejection.

packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts:243 — eventManager.create runs before the payment success update, so a per-host calendar failure makes Stripe retry the webhook and duplicate events on the hosts that already succeeded.

packages/features/ee/payments/api/paypal-webhook.ts:170 — Same retry duplication: create() precedes the payment success update, so a partial multi-host failure produces duplicate calendar events on PayPal's retry.
apps/web/pages/api/cron/bookingReminder.ts:133 — No per-booking try/catch, so a single email or DB failure aborts the whole cron loop and the remaining pending bookings get no reminder this run.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — New fallback loads any credential by raw id (`prisma.credential.findUnique({where:{id: destination.credentialId}})`) with no userId/teamId scoping, deliberately bypassing `this.calendarCredentials` — the only boundary that previously guaranteed the OAuth token used to write a calendar event belonged to the organizer, the event type's team, or the org.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:433 — Cancellation is reachable with only a booking `uid` (`userId` may be undefined), and it now loads an arbitrary credential by raw id and calls `deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)` with values taken from the same unverified BookingReference row, with no check the credential belongs to the booking's organizer or any of its hosts.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:517 — updateAllCalendarEvents` hydrates credentials from `BookingReference.credentialId` via an unscoped `findUnique`, so any credential id stored on a booking reference is used to push the reschedule/update payload into that account's calendar without an ownership check.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:993 — The COLLECTIVE fan-out also matches dynamic group bookings (getDefaultEvent's dynamic event is COLLECTIVE), whose participant list comes straight from the unauthenticated `user` field, so one public booking request now writes attacker-authored event content into every named user's destination calendar using their own stored credentials, instead of only users[0]'s as before.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:2296 — webhookData = {...evt}` now carries an array of every collective host's DestinationCalendar row (externalId, i.e. their calendar/email address, plus credentialId and userId) to arbitrary external subscriber URLs; previously only one row was exposed (confirmed by the `destinationCalendar: []` payload assertion in apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the credentialId for video references (it was `result.credentialId` before), so handleCancelBooking's `if (bookingVideoReference.credentialId)` block never runs and cancelled bookings no longer tear down the Zoom/Teams/Cal Video room — the meeting link stays live and joinable after cancellation.

packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:249 — The re-added `log.error("createEvent failed", JSON.stringify(error), calEvent)` serializes the rejected googleapis/Gaxios error, whose own enumerable `config`/`response.config` carries `headers.Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`, writing the host's OAuth access token into application logs on every calendar-create failure — now triggered once per host in the new fan-out.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:759 — The rewritten `loadUsers` catch re-throws raw `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` text as an HttpError 400, and `defaultResponder` returns `err.message` to the caller, exposing internal Prisma model/field/query details to unauthenticated bookers.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:592 — The catch block still builds `message` (naming the credential type, credential userId and bookingId) but the `console.error(message)` call was deleted, so cross-account calendar update failures — including ones using a DB-hydrated credential belonging to another user — now fail completely silently with no audit trail.

apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249 — The only test change in the PR is a fixture shape flip (null to []), which asserts serialization shape and exercises zero of the new multi-host fan-out behavior.

apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:119 — BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED fixtures still expect `destinationCalendar: null` while BOOKING_REJECTED now expects `[]`, so the suite locks in two contradictory empty shapes instead of catching the inconsistency.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without optional chaining and no test covers a Google Meet booking with an empty/absent destinationCalendar; a unit test in packages/core/EventManager.test.ts would catch the TypeError.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:339 — The core new behavior, the per-destination loop in createAllCalendarEvents that fans out a COLLECTIVE booking to every fixed host, has no unit test anywhere (no packages/core/EventManager.test.ts exists).

The subsequent `calendarId: calendarId || defaultCalendarId` then falls back to `"primary"`, meaning deletions may target the wrong calendar when `externalCalendarId` isn’t provided.
